channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Orders Comprehensive Audit of Defense Ministry
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has ordered a comprehensive review of Kazakhstan's Ministry of Defense. The commission is tasked with examining financial and logistical aspects of military units and must report initial findings to the president within seven days.

item.title: Four Railway Stations Opened in Ulytau Region After Modernization
item.description: Four modernized railway stations have reopened for passengers in Kazakhstan's Ulytau region, located in Zhezkazgan, Karazhal, Zhanarkol, and Kyzylzhar. This initiative is part of a national project to renovate 125 railway stations across the country.

item.title: Explosion in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan kills at least 11, injures 20
item.description: An explosion at a police checkpoint in Dera Ismail Khan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Pakistan, killed at least 11 people and injured 20. The victims included men, women, and a child. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Zhezkazgan-Kyzylorda Road to Open in Coming Months
item.description: The modernization of the Zhezkazgan-Kyzylorda highway is 90% complete and expected to open for traffic in the coming months, according to Ulytau region governor Eset Baiken. Work on the Zhezkazgan-Karaganda section will finish this year, and the Ulytau-Arkalyk road repair will conclude in October.

item.title: Former Kazakh Navy Commander: Caspian Sea Exercises Should Have Been Postponed
item.description: Former Commander of the Kazakh Navy, Vice-Admiral Zhandarbek Zhanzakov, believes military leaders are responsible for the deaths of 14 servicemen during Caspian Sea exercises. He stated the exercises should have been postponed or canceled due to worsening weather conditions.

item.title: Children's Ombudsman Demands Action After Kindergarten Sexual Assault in Namangan
item.description: Uzbekistan's Children's Ombudsman has submitted a request to the Ministry of Preschool and School Education regarding a sexual assault case in a Namangan kindergarten. The ombudsman demands strengthened child safety measures, staff background checks, and revised internal control mechanisms in all kindergartens.

item.title: Kazakh Police Contact Users Criticizing Caspian Incident Online
item.description: Several Kazakh social media users reported being contacted by police after posting critical comments about a recent Caspian Sea incident. One user shared an audio recording of a police officer requesting the removal of a post deemed 'against the people' and aimed at preventing protests.

item.title: Uzbekistan Delegation Attends International Training on Medical Devices in Beijing
item.description: A delegation from Uzbekistan participated in the 5th GHWP (China) Academy international training in Beijing, focusing on advanced medical devices for global public health. The event covered medical device regulation, international harmonization, and innovative medical technologies, offering opportunities to study international experience.

item.title: Business Development Bank Holds Dialogue with Entrepreneurs in Andijan Region
item.description: The Business Development Bank held a dialogue with entrepreneurs in the Andijan region, focusing on supporting business growth, effective investment, and improving banking services. The bank aims to be a financial partner for businesses, assisting with expansion, new projects, equipment acquisition, job creation, and export market entry.

item.title: Graffiti Appears in Almaty Commemorating Soldiers Lost in Caspian Sea Incident
item.description: A graffiti artwork has appeared in Almaty to commemorate 14 soldiers who died during a military exercise in the Caspian Sea on September 24. The artwork depicts the sea, a setting sun, and 14 birds, with the inscription "24.09 Unforgettable. Aktau." Five military officials were detained following the incident.

item.title: Comprehensive Inspection of Defense Ministry Operations Ordered by President
item.description: A special commission has been established by order of the Head of State to conduct a comprehensive assessment of the situation within Kazakhstan's Ministry of Defense. The commission will thoroughly examine the ministry's activities and evaluate the organization and current state of its work.

item.title: Kazakh President Orders Comprehensive Audit of the Ministry of Defense
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has signed a decree to conduct a comprehensive inspection of the Ministry of Defense. A commission has been formed to oversee this audit, comprising high-ranking officials from the Security Council, Supreme Audit Chamber, Presidential Administration, and other key government bodies.

item.title: Tokayev Establishes Commission for Comprehensive Audit of Defense Ministry
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has formed a commission tasked with conducting a comprehensive audit of the Ministry of Defense. This directive indicates a significant review of the ministry's operations and management.

item.title: Tokayev Congratulates Timur Turlov on Election as FIDE President
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated Timur Turlov, president of the Kazakhstan Chess Federation, on his election as president of the International Chess Federation (FIDE). The head of state wished Turlov success in his new role, expressing confidence in his contributions to global chess development.

item.title: Kazakh President Orders Comprehensive Audit of Ministry of Defense
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has ordered the creation of a commission to conduct a comprehensive audit of the Ministry of Defense's affairs. The audit will examine financial and logistical support for military units, with specific officials appointed to lead the commission.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Congratulates Timur Turlov on FIDE Presidency
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev sent a congratulatory telegram to businessman Timur Turlov on his election as president of the International Chess Federation (FIDE). Tokayev wished Turlov success in his new role. Turlov, who also heads the Kazakhstan Chess Federation, was elected in Samarkand with 110 out of 196 votes, succeeding Arkady Dvorkovich.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Labor Market Sees Growing Demand for Skilled Professionals
item.description: Kazakhstan's labor market is evolving, with increasing emphasis on in-demand skills and stronger ties between employers and training systems. Digital tools facilitate faster job searches. By Q2 2026, 9.4 million people were employed, with unemployment at 4.5%. The government aims to increase quality jobs to 3.8 million by 2029.

item.title: Tokayev Congratulates Turlov on Election as FIDE President
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev sent a congratulatory telegram to Timur Turlov, president of the Kazakhstan Chess Federation, on his election as president of the International Chess Federation (FIDE). The head of state wished his compatriot success in leading the prestigious global organization.

item.title: Afghan Freedom Front Reports Clashes with Taliban in Nuristan
item.description: The Afghan Freedom Front claims clashes with Taliban forces began Saturday morning in Kamdish district, Nuristan province, and are ongoing. The group alleges the Taliban attacked its positions with ground forces and drones. The Freedom Front stated its forces defended and launched a counter-attack, capturing several Taliban outposts and pushing them back from certain areas.

item.title: Personnel Changes in Mangystau Region, Kazakhstan
item.description: Several new officials have been appointed at regional, city, and district levels in Kazakhstan's Mangystau region on Saturday, September 26. Yerbol Izbergenov was appointed First Deputy Governor of Mangystau Region. Makasat Mukash is the new mayor of Aktau city, and Symbat Toretayev is the new mayor of Zhanaozen city. New district governors were also appointed.

item.title: Children's Ombudsman Submits Proposal to Ministry Over Kindergarten Abuse Case
item.description: The Children's Ombudsman has submitted a proposal to the Ministry of Preschool and School Education regarding a sexual abuse case involving a child at a kindergarten. The proposal calls for a critical review of the ongoing investigation, addressing identified shortcomings, and holding responsible employees accountable. It also emphasizes strengthening child safety measures across all preschool institutions.

item.title: Taliban Report Seizure of 130 Kilograms of Drugs in Badakhshan
item.description: Taliban authorities in Badakhshan province announced the arrest of four individuals on drug trafficking charges. Approximately 130 kilograms of drugs and two firearms were seized. The Ministry of Interior stated the individuals were identified and arrested in the Tashkan district. Drug trafficking remains a significant challenge in Afghanistan.

item.title: Over 10,000 Subscribers in Kyrgyzstan's Chuy Region to Face Power Disconnections
item.description: More than 10,000 electricity subscribers in Kyrgyzstan's Chuy region will be remotely disconnected due to outstanding debts. The regional power grid enterprise announced planned disconnections for September 28-30, urging residents to pay their bills promptly.

item.title: Tajikistan's Hotel and Restaurant Revenue Surges Nearly 55% in First Half of Year
item.description: In the first six months of this year, the turnover of public catering, hotel services, restaurants, and cafes in Tajikistan reached 2.43 billion somoni. This represents a nearly 55% increase compared to the same period last year.

item.title: Kazakhstan's 'Saltanat Law': Less Than 1% of Violence Complaints Reach Criminal Court
item.description: Under Kazakhstan's 'Saltanat Law,' less than one percent of the 88,000 reported cases of violence against women proceed to criminal court. The law aims to address domestic violence, but statistics indicate a significant gap between reported incidents and judicial action.

item.title: Kazakhstan Celebrates Labor Day: 9.4 Million People Employed in the Economy
item.description: Kazakhstan marks Labor Day on September 27, with 9.4 million people currently employed. The government prioritizes job creation, professional training, labor rights protection, safe working conditions, and skill enhancement. This day honors the contributions of workers to societal and economic development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Allocates 8.5 Billion Som for School Textbook Publication
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has allocated 8.5 billion som from the state budget for the publication of school textbooks. President Sadyr Japarov signed a decree establishing measures for textbook provision, including a program for 2027-2030 and an interdepartmental commission for curriculum review. Measures aim to create a unified system for textbook preparation and distribution.

item.title: Kazakhstan's machine building sector sees 21.2% production growth in January-August
item.description: Production volume in Kazakhstan's machine building sector increased by 21.2% in January-August compared to the same period last year. Over 68,000 people are employed in the industry, which includes automotive, railway, and agricultural machinery manufacturing.

item.title: Turkish and Iranian Foreign Ministers Meet in New York
item.description: Turkey's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan met with his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. While details were not released, discussions likely covered regional issues, Middle East developments, and Iran-US tensions.

item.title: National Security Committee detains 29 suspects with weapons and ammunition
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) has detained 29 individuals suspected of possessing illegal weapons. The seized items include 25 firearms, grenades, and hundreds of rounds of ammunition. Further details on the operation and the suspects' alleged activities were not immediately available.

item.title: Schools in Semey illegally published personal data of over 4,000 individuals
item.description: The prosecutor's office in Semey discovered that 31 schools illegally published the personal data of over 4,000 teachers and students on their official websites. The exposed information included full names, IINs, birth dates, addresses, and phone numbers. The data has been removed, and responsible parties are being held accountable.

item.title: Tajik Prime Minister and Azerbaijani President Discuss Transit and Flights
item.description: Tajik Prime Minister Qohir Rasulzoda and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev discussed Tajikistan's transit of goods through the Middle Corridor. They also reviewed direct flights between Dushanbe and Baku.

item.title: Kazakhstan National Security Committee Detains 29 in Organized Crime Operation
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee, along with the Interior Ministry and under prosecutor coordination, detained 29 individuals in a nationwide operation against organized crime groups. Authorities seized 25 weapons, two grenades, and 236 ammunition rounds.

item.title: Namangan Police Uncover 15 Crimes, Arrest 6 Fugitives, Seize Illegal Items
item.description: During rapid operations in Namangan, police solved 15 crimes and apprehended six fugitives. Authorities also found illegal items on 103 individuals, including 35 cold weapons, 4 firearms, 2 pneumatic weapons, and over 400 grams of narcotics.

item.title: Uzbekistan Needs AI Investment and Local Model Development, Experts Advise
item.description: Experts at ICT Week Uzbekistan recommended investing in education and local AI models over the next five years to cultivate an AI-native generation. They emphasized fostering local startups for global expansion and close private sector collaboration.

item.title: Kyrgyz Akyn Dedicates Lament Song to Fallen Kazakh Soldiers
item.description: Kyrgyz akyn Nursultan Maldybaev has composed and performed a lament song titled 'Konul Aituu' to express condolences to Kazakhstan following the deaths of 14 servicemen at sea. The tragedy occurred during naval exercises when 17 soldiers were swept into the open sea due to sudden bad weather. Three were rescued, and the remaining 14 perished.

item.title: Tashkent Council Orders Traffic Police to Develop Plan to Reduce Fatal Accidents
item.description: The Tashkent City Council has instructed the traffic police (YHXB) to develop a plan within a week to prevent fatal road accidents. This directive follows a report where the council found the traffic police's performance satisfactory but noted the need for targeted measures. A similar order was issued in early 2025.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Niger establish diplomatic relations at UN General Assembly
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev met with his Nigerien counterpart Bakary Yaou Sangare on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly session in New York. The two officials signed a joint communique establishing diplomatic relations between the two countries.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Special operations conducted in ten regions, 29 detained
item.description: Special operations targeting organized crime groups were carried out in ten regions of Kazakhstan. The National Security Committee reported that 29 individuals were detained on suspicion of serious crimes, with nine placed in pre-trial detention. Authorities seized 25 weapons and ammunition.

item.title: Chinese Company to Hire 18 for Gold Exploration in Kazakhstan's Karaganda Region
item.description: Dostyq Minerals, a company owned by Kazakhstan Tianshan Mining Co. Ltd., plans geological exploration for gold at the Araltobe field in the Shet district of Kazakhstan's Karaganda region. The company obtained a license for three blocks totaling 6.88 square kilometers on March 1, 2022, and will hire 18 people for the project.
